subsystems.name: Mass stream or rotor loop
subsystems.role: the moving momentum carrier — its kinetic energy, not the strength of a static member, holds the structure up.
parts: pellets or a continuous composite rotor

subsystems.name: Accelerator and pump stations
subsystems.role: keep the stream at speed, replacing energy lost to friction, deflection and any load it carries.

subsystems.name: Deflector and return stations
subsystems.role: turn the stream around at each end and hand its momentum to the structure.

subsystems.name: Containment sleeve
subsystems.role: evacuated or shielded tube that guides the stream and carries the attached payload — the visible structure.

subsystems.name: Control and damping system
subsystems.role: senses stream position and phase and actively damps oscillation, so the whole assembly behaves as a stiff member.

subsystems.name: Power and thermal system
subsystems.role: supplies the megawatts to gigawatts the drives need and removes heat from magnets and bearings.

buildSteps.title: Fix the geometry and load
buildSteps.detail: Choose the span, the altitude and the useful load, then work out the required stream speed and mass flow so that momentum transfer balances gravity or the applied force.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the sleeve
buildSteps.detail: Make the containment tube in many identical sections, each stiff enough to hold its shape between supports but light enough that most of the load is carried by the stream rather than the shell.

buildSteps.title: Build the end stations
buildSteps.detail: At each end, assemble a curved deflector arc, its magnets and the bearing surface that transfers the stream's redirected momentum into the structure.

buildSteps.title: Install the drives
buildSteps.detail: Line the sleeve with electromagnetic pump sections and their power and cooling feeds, spaced so the stream never slows below the speed the design requires.

buildSteps.title: Thread and spin up the stream
buildSteps.detail: Feed the rotor or pellet stream into the sleeve, then raise its speed gradually with the drives, watching for the resonances that appear as it approaches operating velocity.

buildSteps.title: Pump down and cool
buildSteps.detail: Close and evacuate the tube — or, in orbit, fit shielding — and bring magnets and bearings to operating temperature.

buildSteps.title: Tune the control loop
buildSteps.detail: Measure stream position and phase at many points along the run, then tune the actuators and damping until oscillation stays bounded under the design loads.

buildSteps.title: Load the structure
buildSteps.detail: Attach the payload — tower sections, platforms or a launch track — and increase the load in steps, verifying that deflection and vibration stay within limits.

buildSteps.title: Operate and maintain
buildSteps.detail: Continuously replenish pellets or re-tension the rotor, replace worn deflector surfaces, and keep the drives running during power interruptions using stored energy.

prerequisites.why: carbon-fibre and steel rotors work in principle, but mass ratios decide whether the sleeve can hold together.
the principle is proven in maglev and accelerators; continuous high-duty-cycle drives at the needed scale are not.
accelerator beam pipes and vacuum pipelines show how to hold a long evacuated channel; a megastructure-sized one has not been built.
a stream moving at kilometres per second must be kept phased; active damping is demonstrated only at bench and maglev scale.

prerequisites.tech: Space assembly and large power sources
prerequisites.why: an orbital version means building kilometres of structure in space and supplying gigawatts continuously.
micrometeoroids and debris would puncture a thin vacuum tube unless it is armoured or segmented.

pathway.milestone: bench demonstrations: electromagnetic deflection of fast-moving masses and active damping of flexible structures
pathway.unlocks: confidence that momentum transfer can be controlled tightly enough to be useful.

pathway.milestone: a sealed test loop where a recirculating stream holds a load for hours
pathway.unlocks: proof that the control loop keeps the stream stable under changing load.

pathway.milestone: a small free-flying demonstrator in orbit, a few hundred metres tall
pathway.unlocks: experience with assembly, power and maintenance in vacuum.

pathway.milestone: a full-scale orbital ring or launch loop, thousands of kilometres long
pathway.unlocks: low-cost access to orbit and a platform for very large structures — proposed concepts of this kind date from the early 1980s but remain paper designs.
